items.followUp: What is an enzyme, and how does it affect the rate of a reaction?

rubric.why: An enzyme is a biological catalyst.
rubric.description: Identifies an enzyme as a catalyst.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an enzyme as a biological catalyst.

rubric.why: Enzymes speed up reactions, commonly by lowering their activation energy.
rubric.description: States the effect of an enzyme on a reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an enzyme speeds up a reaction or lowers its activation energy.

modelAnswer: An enzyme is a biological catalyst.
It speeds up a biochemical reaction by lowering its activation energy and is not used up in the reaction.

items.followUp: How does an inhibitor affect an enzyme and its reaction?

rubric.why: An inhibitor reduces or prevents enzyme activity, slowing or stopping the reaction.
rubric.description: States the effect of an inhibitor on enzyme activity or reaction rate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an inhibitor decreases enzyme activity or slows or stops the reaction.

rubric.why: An inhibitor can block the active site or alter the enzyme's shape, preventing effective substrate binding.
rubric.description: Explains how an inhibitor interferes with enzyme action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing an inhibitor binding to the enzyme and blocking the active site, preventing substrate binding, or changing the enzyme's shape.

modelAnswer: An inhibitor is a substance that decreases or stops the activity of an enzyme.
It may bind to the enzyme and block its active site, or change the enzyme's shape so the substrate cannot bind effectively.
